definition: A gameweek in which a player produces no meaningful FPL return beyond ordinary appearance points, or scores no points at all.
caveat: It does not imply that the player was absent or injured.

definition: A large FPL score, normally produced by multiple returns, bonus points or an unusually valuable single performance.
caveat: There is no official points threshold for a haul.

definition: An FPL-relevant scoring contribution such as a goal, assist or clean sheet, depending on position and context.
caveat: Community usage is informal and sometimes excludes appearance points.

definition: Community shorthand for a player believed to have a very secure place in the starting XI.
caveat: It is a confidence judgement, not a guarantee of starting or playing 60 minutes.

definition: Expected minutes: a probability-weighted estimate of how long a player is likely to play, including the chance of not appearing.
caveat: It is an uncertain forecast rather than a promised number of minutes.

definition: A relatively low-owned player whose points can separate a manager from relevant opponents.
caveat: Low ownership alone does not make a player a good pick.

definition: The group of highly owned or commonly selected players that appears across many active squads.
caveat: Template status describes ownership, not whether the players remain optimal.

definition: A low-cost selection used to free budget for more expensive players elsewhere while still providing acceptable minutes or points.
caveat: An enabler still has an opportunity cost and should not be selected solely for price.

definition: A minimum-price or very cheap squad player selected mainly to satisfy squad structure or budget constraints.
caveat: A non-playing fodder pick can weaken autosub resilience.

definition: Ownership adjusted for captaincy and similar multipliers within a relevant manager population, representing rank exposure to a player's score.
caveat: It describes covariance with opponents and is not evidence that the player will score well.

definition: The points cost paid when a manager makes more transfers than their available free transfers permit.
caveat: A transfer should be compared with rolling and must overcome both the hit and future-state opportunity cost.

definition: Make no transfer and carry an available free transfer into a later gameweek when the active rules permit it.
caveat: The current transfer-carry limit must be retrieved from the active-season rules.

definition: A short substitute appearance, often too brief to earn the 60-minute appearance point or clean-sheet eligibility.
caveat: Any appearance can still block an autosub under the relevant rules.

definition: Expected goal involvements, usually the sum of expected goals and expected assists over a stated period or per-90 basis.
caveat: The metric is descriptive evidence and does not automatically account for future minutes or fixtures.

definition: A point in the schedule where one or more clubs move from a difficult fixture run to an easier one, or the reverse.
caveat: Fixture difficulty and the useful planning horizon must be stated rather than assumed.

definition: A gameweek in which a club has more than one fixture allocated to the same FPL event.
caveat: Two fixtures do not guarantee two starts or make every player a good selection.

definition: A gameweek in which a club has no fixture allocated to that FPL event.
caveat: Postponements and rescheduling mean the current fixture snapshot is authoritative.

definition: Uncertainty about whether a player starts, appears, reaches key minute thresholds or is substituted early.
caveat: It should be represented probabilistically and updated with timestamped team news.
